_note: The operands two_jobs.compose reads. Every `<OWNER: ...>` is a choice this
implementer may not take; every other value is pinned by ASSESSMENT-249338.md
and re-verified by verify_247941.py before use.
A documentation member starts with `_`. W239533 learned that the hard way:
its composer splatted a template carrying prose into a keyword call and the
owner's live run met a TypeError. `two_jobs.compose` refuses an unresolved
choice by name and reads no `_` member.
Every operand two_jobs.INSTANCE_OPERANDS and JOB_OPERANDS name is present here; compose refuses by name if they drift apart.

_arrangement: ONE manager, ONE pool, one baton.v12.stage-execution-deployment/2 document
with four stage workers and two job_bindings. Not two isolated managers:
two managers would prove two single-Job deployments still work, which
W239528 and W239533 already established one at a time, and would say
nothing about shared capacity, per-Job allocation or cross-Job isolation.

instance._note: FRESH ROOTS. No consumed 244216 or 248377 store is reused, and no old root is removed.
instance.run_root: <OWNER: an absolute FRESH run root for this two-Job run; it must not exist.>
instance.authority_store: <OWNER: the Authority store this deployment resolves its four participants against.>
instance.job_store: <OWNER: an absolute path for this run's own Job store, under the run root.>
instance.integration_store: <OWNER: an absolute integration store path, outside the checkout.>
instance.state_root: <OWNER: an absolute deployment-state root, outside the checkout.>
instance.workspace_storage: <OWNER: absolute persistent workspace storage on real disk, not a tmpfs.>
instance.credential_sources: <OWNER: absolute private per-user credential registry; null is refused.>
instance.provider_network: <OWNER: the bounded egress network name. `none` is refused: both workers reach an external Claude API.>
instance.retention_policy_digest: <OWNER: the retention policy every intaken artifact is decided under.>
instance.checkpoint_profile: <OWNER: the checkpoint profile name, e.g. git>
instance.job_work_id: <OWNER: the instance-level Work; _MEMBERS requires it even in a /2 document, and job_bindings is what actually binds each Job>
instance.review_work_id: <OWNER: the instance-level review Work, equal to job_work_id>
instance.canonical_target_id: <OWNER: the canonical target both lines publish against>
instance.policy_digest: <OWNER: the Job and input manifest's exact policy digest>
instance.adapter_name: <OWNER: the deployment's fixed OCI adapter name>
instance.engine: <OWNER: docker or podman; only docker is certified>
instance.credential_slots: <OWNER: the closed list of logical slot names, e.g. ["api"]>

instance.submission_id: <OWNER: a fresh submission identity for this run>
